messages:
Luca (New Hire): Hi team, quick international onboarding questions from my first week in Lisbon:
1) My offer referenced a "local pension" option vs Redwood 401(k). Am I auto-enrolled into the Portuguese system or do I opt into a company plan?
2) I paid for temporary storage in EUR while moving — can I submit that for relocation? Will reimbursement be in USD or EUR?
3) My bank in Europe needs an IBAN for reverse charge reimbursements; ADP only shows US routing/account fields. How do I get reimbursed to my EU account?
4) Public holidays: I saw company holiday list is US-centric. Do I get Portugal national holidays?

Hannah (People Ops): Welcome Luca :wave: Short answers:
1) For international hires we typically use local statutory pension (if mandatory) and offer a local voluntary plan if applicable. For Portugal we'll enroll you in the local system (SS) and we don't force Redwood 401(k). If you'd like voluntary top-up options we can discuss vendor choices.
2) Temporary storage is covered under relocation policy if it's within the policy window and listed in your relocation addendum. Reimbursements follow the currency you submit in the portal; Finance prefers local currency for local vendors. We'll convert to USD for reporting but pay out in EUR if you supply an EU bank account.
3) For EU payouts DM @Diego your IBAN and SWIFT; he can open an international reimbursement workflow. ADP sometimes lacks fields for IBAN for certain countries so we use Finance's international ACH process.
4) Remote employees follow the holiday calendar for their country on file. We'll add Portugal national holidays to your profile.

Luca (New Hire): Thanks! For #2, I uploaded a PDF but the portal flagged "currency mismatch" because invoice is EUR but I selected USD. How should I re-file?

Sophie (Benefits): Hey Luca  re-file the expense and choose EUR as currency. If the portal won't accept EUR, upload the invoice and add a short note in the comments with the EUR amount; tag us and we'll convert and process manually. Include the vendor invoice number to speed review.

Diego (Payroll): Luca  DM me the IBAN/SWIFT and your preferred payout currency. For future payroll-styled taxable stipends we still need local tax treatment; I might need to consult with our EOR (employer-of-record) partner for Portugal specifics. Expect a 3-7 business day processing time for international ACH.

Luca (New Hire): Curious about tax treaties  if I remain a Portuguese tax resident but also have US-source stock vesting, will Redwood withhold US taxes? Is there a treaty step?

Hannah (People Ops): That's a bit gray and depends on residency and source rules. Payroll will likely withhold per US rules for RSUs, but you may be eligible for treaty relief or credits on your Portuguese return. @Diego can loop in tax advisors for a definitive answer.

Diego (Payroll): Correct  RSU and equity withholding is nuanced. I'll escalate to Tax Ops and the EOR partner. In the meantime, DM me the equity vest date and we'll flag it so you don't get surprised on payout.

Luca (New Hire): Appreciate it. Last small Q  floating day policy: if Portuguese national holidays exceed US count, do we get extra local floating days or just the local list?

Sophie (Benefits): Remote employees get the local statutory holidays; floating days are prorated and applied per country policy. If you have more local holidays than the base US calendar, we'll reflect those on your profile rather than subtracting.

Global HR Bot: Note: international benefit enrollments require ID verification and local tax docs within 30 days of start. Failure to supply may delay vendor enrollment. Guidance: https://intranet.redwood.com/intl-onboarding

Luca (New Hire): Great, thanks everyone. I'll DM Diego my IBAN and upload corrected EUR invoices. Happy to be here! :tada:
